units.text: The WHO African Region accounted for approximately 94-95% of global malaria cases in 2024, not 75% as claimed. Multiple authoritative sources state 94% or 95% of cases were in the African Region.

citations.title: Malaria facts & statistics 2025 | Medicines for Malaria Venture

judgement.reason: The passages state the WHO African Region accounted for 94% or 95% of global malaria cases in 2024, and the only 75% figure refers to under-5 deaths in the region, not global cases, so the statement is supported.

units.text: The 75% figure in the assertion contradicts the consistent 94-95% estimate across WHO and MMV reports for 2024 African Region case share.

judgement.reason: The passages state 94-95% of African Region cases/deaths and separately mention 75% of deaths as under-5, but they do not contain an assertion using 75% for case share, nor any MMV report, so they cannot establish that a 75% figure contradicts the 94-95% case-share estimate.

units.text: The African Region's share of malaria cases has remained around 94-95% in recent WHO reports, far exceeding the 75% claimed in the assertion.

judgement.reason: The passages show the African Region had 94-95% of malaria cases in 2024, which far exceeds 75%, but they only give 2024 data and do not establish that this share has remained around 94-95% across recent WHO reports over time.
